# PLAN — iteration 4
## Current state assessment
The verified incumbent is already timing-feasible at 7 LUTs, 9 FFs, WNS 0.553 ns, and WHS 0.135 ns, so this iteration must strictly reduce LUTs (or tie LUTs and reduce FFs) while passing every gate. The previous 8-bit up-counter variants were rejected at 10–11 LUTs; repeating those patterns has no evidence of improving the objective. The top’s numeric latency is unknown, so no numeric annotation is required.

## Hypothesis
Complementing the 8-bit phase state and counting downward may map the modulo counter and PWM comparison to fewer LUTs while preserving the same 0–255 phase sequence and registered output behavior.

## Instruction for generator
Replace the 32-bit up-counter with an 8-bit complemented phase register, reset it to `8'hFF`, and decrement it unconditionally on each non-reset clock. Compute `pwm_out` from the old phase using the equivalent unsigned comparison `phase > ~duty`, preserving the existing synchronous reset of `pwm_out` and its registered update. Keep the interface and cycle behavior unchanged; promote the candidate only if verification passes and routed metrics meet the required strict objective comparison against the incumbent.
